text:
dan (bench): quick share — ran a multi-region warmup/edge-split comparison across US-EAST / US-WEST / EU-WEST for redwood-v1 quantized 4-bit. attached CSV and p50/p95 snapshots.

alexa (ml-eng): nice, did you vary kernel types (flash vs triton) and batch sizes?

dan (bench): yep. matrix: H100 vs A100, kernels=flash,triton, batch sizes 1/4/8, seq=128/256. only changed routing: baseline all->nearest, test->force US-WEST edge for 30m.

benji (infra): high-level numbers?

dan (bench): p50 (us-east/us-west/eu-west) = 18ms / 22ms / 28ms; p95 = 120ms / 260ms / 410ms for H100+flash q4, bs=4, seq=128. notable p95 blow-up in EU-WEST when routed via us-west edge.

carla (sre): 410ms p95… that's big. any tails from kernel fallback or bench noise?

dan (bench): looked at logs: during the forced us-west routing window eu-west requests hit a proxy that had intermittent SYN retries -> added ~150-300ms hop penalty + cold KV-cache misses for short chats. Also triton kernel showed ~10-15% worse p95 but slightly better throughput for large bs.

alexa (ml-eng): so p50 stays fine but p95 dominated by network/hop + cold cache. did you try prefix/KV warmup?

dan (bench): yes — warmup (1000 calls/region with same prompt set) reduced eu-west p95 410 -> 180ms, p50 unchanged. implies caching + edge path matters a lot.

benji (infra): capacity sizing note: for H100 we saw steady qps/GPU ~220 for seq=128 bs=4 q4; A100 ~170. With p95 SLO target 250ms, EU-West would need 1.6x overcommit if routing via US-West edge.

carla (sre): ops suggestion: prefer regional routing for EU traffic unless we know edge path is warm and healthy. add circuit-breaker if hop latency > 80ms for >1m. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: benchmark artifact uploaded: https://redwood.internal/bench/2084729001 (charts + CSV).

alexa (ml-eng): any quality regressions from q4 quant? We care if quant trade-off is worth perf gain.

dan (bench): small delta on rouge/bertscore for our eval set: avg BERTScore down 0.6 pts. for safety gate we'll keep q4 for high-throughput non-critical routes, and use fp16 for high-quality paths.

benji (infra): kernel notes: flash-attn gives micro-ops benefit on H100; triton fallback was triggered when seq > 1024 or certain kv-cache sizes — we saw the runtime pick triton for some long-tail prompts which raised p95. tweak: pin kernel=flash for short sequences to keep tail low.

carla (sre): can we add a heatmap to console: region x edge-path showing p95 delta & cache-hit%? ops-bot, flag as postmortem candidate if routing change caused user-facing SLO breaches.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-6732 and added alert rule candidate: p95_region > 300ms for 5min -> page oncall.

dan (bench): command I used to reproduce locally if you want to run quick checks:
```
./bench --model redwood-v1 --gpu h100 --region eu-west --route-force us-west-edge --qbits 4 --bs 4 --seq 128 --duration 1800 --prom-url http://prom:9090
```

alexa (ml-eng): plan: 1) enforce regional routing by default, 2) add warmup run when switching edge path, 3) expose kernel pinning in rollout flags. I'll open a PR for rollout flag and doc.

benji (infra): I'll add a synthetic warmup job to run 5m after route changes and a quick hop-latency probe.

carla (sre): TL;DR for ops playbook: warm caches + prefer local edge = keeps p95 in target. routing to remote edge doubles/triples tail.

dan (bench): thanks — will drop CSV + raw logs in the ticket. short follow-up: for throughput planning, assume EU-West H100 capacity ~200 qps/GPU steady, and pad 1.5x for SLO headroom when cross-edge routing is possible. :eyes:
